regressions.source: Vault.sol: sellUSDG(address _token, address _receiver); decreasePosition(..., address _receiver); liquidatePosition(..., address _feeReceiver)
regressions.issue: The receiver parameter is now typed uint256 where the old text typed it address, as the ABI does. Its use as a transfer argument is now the byte slices uint128(_p >> 32) and uint32(_p), which hides the address mask.
regressions.rule: Infer a parameter's type from the value its uses compute: slices that together make the low 160 bits of _p are an address use. Merging the slices (new finding 1) fixes this too.

regressions.decompiled: if POS.field_256 >= _param4: (if POS.field_1024: ... mul ...) _1049 = _1044 / else: (revert with stor48[33] ...)
regressions.issue: A guard that only reverts is now printed as the else arm of an if/else, after the main path it protects, with a negated condition (P10). The old text put the guard first. Old text 0 such else-arm reverts, new 4.
regressions.rule: When one arm of a branch only reverts, print it first as a one-armed 'if cond: revert', with the other arm after it, whatever the arms' order in the CFG.

new_findings.decompiled: call address(_param1).transfer(address recipient, uint256 amount) with: args Bytes(28, uint128(_param2 >> 32)), Bytes(4, uint32(_param2)), (...) / 10000
new_findings.issue: The transfer is now named, but its recipient is shown as two byte slices of the parameter rather than address(_param2). The other path's transfer in the same function prints address(_param7). The slices come from the selector's read-modify-write of the word that overlaps the address.
new_findings.rule: Merge adjacent slices of one value: Bytes(28, uint128(x >> 32)) followed by Bytes(4, uint32(x)) is the 32-byte word x & (2**160 - 1), i.e. address(x). In general, Bytes(a, (x >> 8b) mod 2**(8(a-k))) ++ Bytes(b, x mod 2**(8b)) is Bytes(a + b, x mod 2**(8(a+b-k))).
new_findings.verified: reading only (exact: the two slices concatenate to the masked word)

The mul revert data are exact, past the message too (round-1 finding 1 fixed; text_check 0 different, round 1 had 5). The position key at an unknown pointer is resolved, so every member is stor43[key].field_N (274 raw slots -> 0, P4 24 -> 0). P6 309 -> 0. P2 16 -> 2: sellUSDG's transfer, balanceOf, its event and its return are decoded, and vaultUtils.validateLiquidation (0xfdaf6ac3) is decoded in decreasePosition and liquidatePosition. notes: The diff is 15421 lines, so this is a structural review. Functions were reordered: liquidatePosition (hunks 46/101), getRedemptionAmount and others moved. I compared each of the 15 changed defs old-vs-new: buyUSDG, sellUSDG, swap and the 3 position functions by calls, events, storage writes, reverts and loops; the small ones (SafeMath block, getRedemptionAmount, getRedemptionCollateral, getRedemptionCollateralUsd, getNextGlobalShortAveragePrice, getNextAveragePrice, updateCumulativeFundingRate, clearTokenConfig, directPoolDeposit) line by line. Every call and log keeps its count in every function. Storage-write differences are only -= turned into = SafeMath.sub and raw slots turned into fields. require ext_code.size(vaultUtils) dropped from 16 to 7 in decreasePosition (also in liquidatePosition and increasePosition). These are repeated checks: every vaultUtils call is still dominated by a check, and each remaining check comes right before a call, so none was hoisted. The extcodesize check hoisted above the branch in getNextAveragePrice is exact, since both arms call priceFeed. updateCumulativeFundingRate now nests ifs where it had early stops: equivalent. The 'x = cond and v' form is not new (28 in the old text). The unsimplified forms 'len _2322 - mem[64] + 132' (where _2322 = mem[64]) also existed before (29 -> 5). A no-op 'stor37[t] = stor37[t]' (poolAmounts.sub(0)) shows in liquidatePosition. Execution: text_check run --seed 6 --random --each --per-selector 8 gives random 475 same, guessed-params 508 same, 0 different.
summary: No semantic regression, and 2 low ones: receiver params now typed uint256, and 4 guards printed as else arms in decreasePosition. A big cleanup: the copy-loop reverts folded, exact mul revert padding (round-1 finding 1 fixed), positions[key] resolved (finding 5 fixed), P2 16 -> 2, -3800 lines. A transfer's recipient is still shown as two byte slices.
